hook.line: India's flicking game: flick the striker and send the men into the four corner pockets.
hook.say: Let me show you India's one-finger game!

ch.say: There's even a glass board in a palace!
p: Carrom is a flicking board game born in the Indian subcontinent. A palace in Patiala still keeps a board whose playing surface is glass.

State tournaments were held across India early in the 20th century, and serious tournaments may have begun in Sri Lanka around 1935. In 1988 the International Carrom Federation was founded in Chennai and the rules were unified.

ch.say: A pinch of powder and everything glides.
ch.cap: A carrom board (ICF size): the base lines in front, the pockets in the corners, the men in the middle
p: The surface is smooth plywood, 74 cm square, with a 4.45 cm pocket in each corner, base lines and red circles on every side, arrows on the diagonals and circles in the middle.
There are 9 white men, 9 black and one red queen (3.18 cm, about 5.5 g). The striker is up to 4.13 cm and 15 g — heavy. Powder on the board makes everything slide.
